description: He asks how to say ταῦτα and his English accent is IPA (the standard): the request's guide gives each sound by its IPA symbol, so the answer says how it sounds in modern Greek (TAF-ta) and gives no English key word.

request.greek: Τεκνία μου ταῦτα γράφω ὑμῖν ἵνα μὴ ἁμάρτητε Καὶ ἐάν τις ἁμάρτῃ παράκλητον ἔχομεν πρὸς τὸν πατέρα Ἰησοῦν χριστὸν δίκαιον
request.english: My little children, I am writing these things to you so that you will not sin. But if anyone does sin, we have an advocate before the Father — Jesus Christ, the Righteous One.
request.question: How do I say ταῦτα?
request.pronunciation_guide: Modern Greek, as Greek is spoken in Greece today: never by English spelling habit and never by the Erasmian (school) pronunciation. The app respells a word in syllables, the stressed one in capitals: ταῦτα is TAF-ta, Πάντοτε is PAN-do-te, χαίρετε is HYE-re-te. The vowels, each by its IPA symbol, with no English word: a, /a/; e, /e/; ee, /i/; o, /o/; oo, /u/. αυ and ευ are af and ef before θ κ ξ π σ τ φ χ ψ, and av and ev before a voiced consonant or a vowel (never "aw", never "ow"); ηυ is eef or eev the same way. αι is e; ει, οι, υι, η, ι and υ are ee; ου is oo; ω and ο are o. β is v; δ is dh, /ð/; γ is gh (or y before ε, ι, η, υ, αι, ει or οι); θ is th, /θ/; φ is f; ρ is r, /ɾ/; χ is kh, /x/, before α, ο, ω, ου or a consonant, and the softer hy before ε, ι, η, υ, αι, ει or οι. μπ, ντ and γκ are b, d and g at the start of a word and mb, nd and ng inside it; γγ is ng; γχ is ng plus kh (or hy before ε, ι, η, υ, αι, ει or οι); γξ is nks. σ is z before β γ δ ζ λ μ ν ρ. A doubled consonant is said once. Both breathings are silent, and the iota under a letter is not said.
